hero.title: Gasifier Syngas Simulator
hero.description: Estimate syngas composition, heating value, and engine power potential based on your gasifier type, fuel, and operating conditions. Results use a simplified equilibrium model — treat them as indicative, not design specifications.

inputs.heading: Inputs
inputs.blendToggleHelp: Mix two fuel species by mass fraction to simulate co-gasification (e.g. charcoal + wood chips).
inputs.blendRatioHelp: Percentage of primary fuel in the blend by dry mass.
inputs.erHelp: ER is the ratio of actual air supplied to stoichiometric air. Most gasifiers run 0.25–0.35.
inputs.engineToggleHelp: Enter your engine's displacement and RPM to see how well it matches this syngas — including derating, fuel feed rate, and shaft power estimate.
inputs.engineDisplacementHelp: Total swept volume of all cylinders. Common genset engines: 400–800 cc (small), 1000–2000 cc (medium), 3000+ cc (large).

compare.heading: Multi-fuel comparison
compare.subheading: Run all fuels at the same conditions and see how they rank.

results.compositionNote: CO + H₂ are the combustible components. N₂ is inert diluent from air.

methodology.heading: About this simulator — work in progress
methodology.body1: This tool uses a simplified two-reaction equilibrium model based on the Boudouard reaction and water-gas shift, with fuel properties drawn from the FAO Forestry Paper 72 and FEMA emergency gasifier documentation.
methodology.body2: Real gasifiers deviate from equilibrium due to reaction kinetics, channeling, tar formation, and heat losses.
methodology.body2Bold: Do not use these numbers for engineering design.
methodology.body2Tail: They are useful for understanding how changes in moisture, fuel type, and equivalence ratio affect syngas quality — not for sizing components or predicting exact output.
methodology.body3: Planned additions: pressure drop, char burnout fraction, engine derating factors, and a fuel drying energy calculator.
